## Goal
The registry refuses YAML aliases to lists or maps (`src/freemyid/registry.py:38-49`), but `checklists.load` (`src/freemyid/checklists.py:22-29`) and `law_matrix.load` (`src/freemyid/engine/law_matrix.py:111-126`) use plain `yaml.safe_load`, so a small file can expand to gigabytes. Neither has a test for a file saved on Windows (UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF line endings), and the matrix accepts any two letters as a state (`MatrixEntry.state`, 37) and silently treats a typo in `evidence` as "not verified".

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Both loaders refuse aliases to lists or maps (a billion-laughs file fails fast and small); aliases to plain scalars still load. Reuse the registry's loader by import (`from ..registry import _NoAliasLoader` or equivalent) without editing `registry.py`, or a small local equivalent; say which in VENDOR_STATUS.md.
2. A UTF-8 file with a BOM and CRLF line endings loads exactly like the plain file in both loaders.
3. `law_matrix.parse` (93-108): an entry whose state is not a US state or DC (use `matcher.STATE_NAMES`, `src/freemyid/engine/matcher.py:66`) or whose `evidence` / `response_days_evidence` is not one of the known values is dropped with a warning naming the state code only; the rest of the matrix still loads, and the fail-closed rule (`citable` 62-67: no citation without verified evidence) holds.
4. Existing behaviour kept: a missing or broken matrix still yields `EMPTY` (`load` 111-126); a missing checklists file still raises `FileNotFoundError` (29).
5. Tests write files under `tmp_path` only.

This is Codex code-lane work (owner, 2026-11-09): fix and improve the listed module(s) directly, with tests; don't xfail a bug you can fix here. No contract changes: public function signatures, `src/freemyid/models.py`, `interfaces.py`, schema files, `--json` shapes and documented CLI output stay as they are (additive helpers inside the listed files are fine). If the work turns out to need a contract change, stop and say so in VENDOR_STATUS.md "Questions for the owner". Fake data only, offline (fake fetchers, no network), Windows-safe paths in tests (`tmp_path`, `pathlib`, no `/tmp`). Typed, ruff-clean, small diff. Line numbers are from main at the time of writing; re-check them.
